newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Asia veg oil demand to rise strongly - Oil World.
newsitem.headline: Asia veg oil demand to rise strongly - Oil World.

text.p: Asian vegetable oils and fat demand is set to rise sharply in the 1996/97 season (Oct/Sept) due to high income and population growth in the region, the Hamburg-based newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.

In a survey of the large Asian consuming countries, China is expected to remain the region's growth leader. Oil World predicted domestic oils and fats offtake would rise by around 900,000 tonnes to 14.3 million tonnes.
Asian growth "will remain significantly above that in most other countries," it said. "In China domestic disappearance of oils/fats has shown exceptionally sharp growth since 1993/94."
But this Chinese growth is slightly lower than this year's 1.15 million tonne-increase in domestic offtake as income growth begins to slow and, more importantly, import prices rise.
A tightening in world supplies and sharp decline in next season's ending stocks of oilseeds, oils and fats in virtually all exporting countries will push prices up considerably.
Oil World also forecast domestic Chinese production would drop by 0.6 percent to 10.1 million tonnes, following similar decreases this and last season.

The fall will heighten the need for imports of oils and fats -- forecast to rise by 3.8 percent to 3.8 million tonnes in 1996/97 -- and a further reduction in stocks -- forecast down to 1.1 million tonnes by the end of next season.
But it said the government would be likely to act before stocks fell below that level to quell any potential impact on prices.

"We believe the Chinese government would not like to see a repetition of the sharp increases in domestic prices, which fuelled inflation, and will therefore do everything to prevent the stocks falling below 1.1 million tonnes," Oil World said. --Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
